text:
sam: Heads up — main CI just went red right after merge of #4321 (kv-cache quickopt), failing e2e job
ci-bot: [ALERT] pipeline main/e2e-gpu-kvcache failed on commit 7f3a2b1 · test_kv_cache_eviction (exit 137)
anya: @sahil did you merge that? any risky changes? :eyes:
sahil: yeah that was my PR, only tweaked perf knobs, didn't touch eviction logic. sorry, landed fast to unblock perf tests.
maria: ok starting quick triage. First step: rerun the failing job, see if transient. i'll kick that off.
maria: /rerun main/e2e-gpu-kvcache job 98765
deploy-bot: Rerun queued by maria — job 98766 (retest from commit 7f3a2b1)
sam: if rerun flakes, we should bisect the small range (7f3a2b1..a1c4d5e) — only 4 merges, quick to check
ci-bot: Rerun completed: job 98766 — FAILED again (exit 137)
anya: logs show OOM inside model loader step, different from eviction failure in unit tests. attaching snippet:
```
[2026-03-17 14:12:33] load_model: Allocating 16GB GPU memory...
[2026-03-17 14:12:34] ERROR: cudaOutOfMemory: Tried to allocate 16384MB at model/shard_loader.cc:412
[2026-03-17 14:12:34] process exited with code 137
```
sahil: hmm I increased batch prefetching in the runtime layer, could raise memory pressure. will revert that commit locally and run the e2e repro
maria: in parallel, @eng-infra can we run the same job with reduced batch_prefetch=1 to see if it passes? that would confirm memory regression
sam: +1. if that passes we can patch config on main quickly then bisect for root cause
ci-bot: New job queued: main/e2e-gpu-kvcache@config=low-prefetch job 98767
deploy-bot: Job 98767 started on gpu-pool-7
anya: also tagging @sre for visibility in case it's infra-side memory scheduling issue
sam: thanks — let's avoid an emergency revert until we get repro. if job 98767 fails too, we'll revert sahil's merge and open a follow-up rollback PR
sahil: i'm already preparing a revert PR just in case. posting link: https://git.redwood/infra/merge-rollback/4321
maria: job 98767 PASSED. looks like prefetch change pushed memory over the edge.
anya: great signal. sahil can you open a small follow-up to reduce prefetch or make it dynamic? also add a unit test that simulates tight memory allocations
sahil: on it. i'll cut a fix PR and include a short note in the release changelog. sorry for the noise everyone. :bow:
